summary: The function now processes the text left‑to‑right, accumulating each character’s cell width and starting a new line whenever adding the next character would exceed the supplied width, returning the resulting lines in the original order. summary: When next_version is called with part="prerelease" and a prerelease_token that differs from the current version’s prerelease token (i.e., version.prerelease is not None and the first token of version.prerelease does not equal prerelease_token), the function now returns a version whose prerelease is set to <prerelease_token>.1 with build cleared, instead of incrementing the numeric suffix of the existing prerelease token as it did before.

title: Fix string_to_int radix when alphabet_index is provided
summary: When an alphabet_index is supplied, string_to_int now computes the radix as len(alphabet_index) instead of len(alphabet), so the base used for conversion changes whenever the two lengths differ. Consequently, inputs such as "010" with alphabet ['0','1','2'] and index {'0':0,'1':1} yield 2 instead of 3, and "20" with alphabet ['0','1'] and index {'0':0,'1':1,'2':2} yield 6 instead of 4.

summary: The function now unconditionally calls self.wait(retry_state) and assigns the result to retry_state.upcoming_sleep. Previously, when self.wait was falsy (e.g., None, False, 0, or an empty list), the function skipped the call and set upcoming_sleep to 0.0. After the change, those same inputs cause a TypeError because the non‑callable value is invoked as a function, while callable wait objects continue to behave as before.

list(split_when([], lambda x, y: True, maxsplit=0))

summary: When maxsplit is 0, split_when now yields the whole iterable as a single sub‑list only if the iterable is non‑empty; for an empty iterable it yields no output, whereas before it always yielded a single empty list [[]]. This change affects any call with maxsplit=0, regardless of the predicate or the type of the iterable.

Revert "Fix humanize reporting 'a month' for 16-day differences"
Fix humanize reporting 'a month' for 16-day differences
summary: The change prevents rounding up to a month when the elapsed time is more than two weeks but less than a full month and no calendar month has fully passed; instead, it returns a weeks‑based description. Consequently, Arrow(2020,1,1).humanize(Arrow(2020,1,20)) now yields '2 weeks ago' rather than 'a month ago'.
